passage:
Maya: Our school is preparing a Future Neighbourhood exhibition. Each team must present one realistic change.
Omar: What will your group demonstrate? I heard some students have chosen electric transport.
Maya: We are designing a model of a community centre powered partly by solar panels with batteries.
Omar: Why choose solar power? Though there is sunshine, weather and maintenance still affect electricity production.
Maya: Exactly. The model shows both sunny and cloudy days, so visitors can compare different energy conditions.
Omar: Will your group promise that the community centre will never need electricity from the grid?
Maya: No. That would be misleading. We will explain they provide support when sunlight is limited.
Omar: Did you consider installing a wind turbine? Some classmates think wind energy works equally well everywhere.
Maya: We discussed it, but wind speeds vary. We cannot recommend a turbine without wind measurements.
Omar: What will happen to the model after the exhibition? Will materials be thrown away.
Maya: The science department will reuse the panels and sensors in lessons, then recycle damaged components properly.
Omar: How will visitors understand the difference between a forecast and a prediction?
Maya: We will display a chart and label all figures as measurements from a classroom model.
Omar: What about people who cannot read small labels?
Maya: We are preparing large-print explanations and an audio description,.
Omar: Are the sensors online? Will personal data be collected.
Maya: The demonstration records light levels only. It does not record faces, voices.
Omar: What date is the exhibition? My cousin is interested in climate science and wants to attend.
Maya: It opens next Wednesday at ten. Families can visit the school hall until two.
Omar: How many teams are involved, and will all of them present the same kind of technology?
Maya: There are six teams. Their topics include transport, renewable electricity, water conservation and digital services.
Omar: Which team will discuss changing employment?.
Maya: The digital services team will examine changing jobs and explain why people may need new skills.
Omar: Will the exhibition decide which technology is best for Oman, or encourage visitors to ask questions?
Maya: We want thoughtful questions. Different communities have different needs, budgets and environmental conditions.
Omar: What will visitors do if they have a suggestion about the models?
Maya: They can complete an anonymous feedback form, and the groups will discuss useful ideas after the event.
Omar: Then I will bring my cousin. Your exhibition sounds more balanced than exaggerated promises.

questions.stem: Why won't the students guarantee complete independence from grid electricity?
options: Batteries and grid power are sometimes needed

questions.stem: Why did the group avoid recommending a wind turbine immediately?
options: They had not measured local wind conditions
The school had banned wind energy

questions.stem: How many teams are preparing displays?
The group's chart distinguishes model measurements from predictions.
Visitors must provide their names when giving suggestions.
The digital services team will discuss changing jobs.
The exhibition claims that one technology is best for every community.

notes: Fictional future-neighbourhood model discussion and renewable energy.
